newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares slither, end weaker, watch govt vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares slither, end weaker, watch govt vote.

text.p: Italian shares ended largely colourless session weaker biding their time ahead of a government confidence vote on the Banco di Napoli restructuring plan.
The Mibtel all-share index finished the day 1.25 percent weaker at 9,890 and the Mib-30 blue-chips index finished 1.4 percent off at 14,917.
Telecoms tumbled sharply after Telecom Italia fell foul of antitrust authority with its plans for advanced cordless phone.
Fiat and Generali slipped amid market sentiment Generali overpaid for Fiat fund manager Prime in a deal announced on Tuesday.

Comments by Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing depressed sentiment in afternoon trade. Issing said there was no reason to expect further cuts in German interest rates, prompting the mark to strengthen against the lira.

The Napoli vote was designed to push through cabinet decree to rescue the bank. Passage of the decree is being threatened by 1,001 amendments submitted by separatist Northern League party. Napoli shares suspended limit-up at 575.4 lire.
Heavy volume in Cofide with one two million share cross trade. Shares finished the day 3.47 percent firmer at 599.1.
Telecom Italia closed 0.97 percent weaker at 3,488. TIM fell 2.61 percent to 3,246 and Stet slid 2.1 percent to 5,411.
Olivetti firmed 4.19 percent at 455.2, bouncing from record low on Tuesday. Olivetti-controlled mobile phone venture Omnitel outstrips TIM in GSM subscriber race.
Fiat ended 1.62 percent off at 4,178 and Generali 2.27 weaker at 30,722.
